22177-morality-as-a-religion.title: An Exposition Of Some First Principles
22177-morality-as-a-religion.creator: Dr. Felix Adle
22177-morality-as-a-religion.description: A book by Dr. Felix Adle. ich makes us one with the Moral Progress of Humanity, by incessant co-operation with "the Power that makes for Righteousness". If Religion be, what its name signifies, the unifying principle of mankind, in no other wise can we be possibly made One with each other and with the Universal Power than by so living as to secure the ends for which worlds and men exist.

arxiv-2011-14995.title: Adapting LIGO workflows to run in the Open Science Grid Journal: SoftwareX
arxiv-2011-14995.creator: Edgar Fajardo, Frank Wuerthwein, Brian Bockelman, Miron Livny, Greg Thain, James Alexander Clark, Peter Couvares, Josh Willis
arxiv-2011-14995.description: Abstract During the first observation run the LIGO collaboration needed to offload some of its most, intense CPU workflows from its dedicated computing sites to opportunistic resources. Open Science Grid enabled LIGO to run PyCbC, RIFT and Bayeswave workflows to seamlessly run in a combination of owned and opportunistic resources.

arxiv-2112-13369.title: Stop Line Aided Cooperative Positioning of Connected Vehicles
arxiv-2112-13369.creator: Xingqi Wang, Chaoyang Jiang, Shuxuan Sheng, Yanjie Xu, and Yifei Jia
arxiv-2112-13369.description: Abstract This paper develops a stop line aided cooperative positioning framework for connected vehicles, which creatively utilizes the location of the stop-line to achieve the positioning enhancement for a vehicular ad-hoc network (VANET) in intersection scenarios via Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication.

arxiv-2204-02912.title: Variational Quantum Evolution Equation Solver
arxiv-2204-02912.creator: Fong Yew Leong, Wei-Bin Ewe, Dax Enshan Koh
arxiv-2204-02912.description: Abstract Variational quantum algorithms offer a promising new paradigm for solving partial differential equations on near-term quantum computers. Here, we propose a variational quantum algorithm for solving a general evolution equation through implicit time-stepping of the Laplacian operator. The use of encoded source states informed by preceding solution vectors results in faster convergence compared to random re-initialization.

arxiv-2208-04217.title: EMISSA - Exploring Millimetre Indicators of Solar-Stellar Activity
arxiv-2208-04217.creator: A. Mohan, S. Wedemeyer, P. H. Hauschildt, S. Pandit, M. Saberi
arxiv-2208-04217.description: Abstract Context. An activity indicator, which can provide a robust quantitative mapping between the stellar activity and the physical properties of its atmosphere, is important in exploring the evolution of the observed active phenomena across main-sequence stars of different spectral types.

arxiv-2310-03647.title: Rethinking Algorithmic Fairness for Human-AI Collaboration Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2310-03647.creator: Haosen Ge, Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania Hamsa Bastani, Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania Osbert Bastani, University of Pennsylvania
arxiv-2310-03647.description: Abstract . Abstract: Existing approaches to algorithmic fairness aim to ensure equitable outcomes if human decision-makers comply perfectly with algorithmic decisions. However, perfect compliance with the algorithm is rarely a reality or even a desirable outcome in human-AI collaboration. Yet, recent studies have shown that selective compliance with fair algorithms can amplify discrimination relative to the prior human policy.

arxiv-2407-20526.title: On the energy barrier of hypergraph product codes
arxiv-2407-20526.creator: Guangqi Zhao, Andrew C. Doherty, Isaac H. Kim
arxiv-2407-20526.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guangqi Zhao, Andrew C. Doherty, Isaac H. Kim. A macroscopic energy barrier is a necessary condition for self-correcting quantum memory. In this paper, we prove tight bounds on the energy barrier applicable to any quantum code obtained from the hypergraph product of two classical codes.

arxiv-2503-14403.title: Landscape Complexity for the Empirical Risk of Generalized Linear Models: Discrimination between Structured Data
arxiv-2503-14403.creator: Theodoros G. Tsironis, Aris L. Moustakas
arxiv-2503-14403.description: Abstract We use the Kac-Rice formula and results from random matrix theory to obtain the average number of critical points of a family of high-dimensional empirical loss functions, where the data are correlated d d -dimensional Gaussian vectors, whose number has a fixed ratio with their dimension.

arxiv-2504-15627.title: ZeroSlide: Is Zero-Shot Classification Adequate for Lifelong Learning in Whole-Slide Image Analysis in the Era of Pathology Vision-Language Foundation Models?
arxiv-2504-15627.creator: Doanh C. Bui, Hoai Luan Pham, Vu Duong Trung Le, Tuan Hai Vu, Van Duy Tran, Yasuhiko Nakashima
arxiv-2504-15627.description: Abstract Lifelong learning for whole-slide images (WSIs) poses the challenge of training a unified model to perform multiple WSI-related tasks, such as cancer subtyping and tumor classification, in a distributed, continual fashion. This is a practical and applicable problem in clinics and hospitals, as WSIs are large, require storage, processing, and transfer time.

arxiv-2512-02745.title: A Note on the Conditions for COS Convergence
arxiv-2512-02745.creator: Qinling Wang, Xiaoyu Shen, Fang Fang
arxiv-2512-02745.description: Abstract We study the truncation error of the COS method and give simple, verifiable conditions that guarantee convergence. In one dimension, COS is admissible when the density belongs to both L1 and L2 and has a finite weighted L2 moment of order strictly greater than one.

arxiv-2512-24136.title: Bicombing the mapping class group and Teichmüller space via stable cubical intervals
arxiv-2512-24136.creator: Matthew Gentry Durham
arxiv-2512-24136.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matthew Gentry Durham. In this mostly expository article, we provide a new account of our proof with Minsky and Sisto that mapping class groups and Teichmüller spaces admit bicombings. More generally, we explain how the hierarchical hull of a pair of points in any colorable hierarchically hyperbolic space is quasi-isometric to a finite CAT(0) cube complex of bounded dimension, with the added property that perturbing the pair of points results in a uniformly bounded change to the cubical structure.

arxiv-2602-23212.title: Through BrokenEyes : How Eye Disorders Impact Face Detection?
arxiv-2602-23212.creator: Prottay Kumar Adhikary
arxiv-2602-23212.description: Abstract Vision disorders significantly impact millions of lives, altering how visual information is processed and perceived. In this work, a computational framework was developed using the BrokenEyes system to simulate five common eye disorders: Age-related macular degeneration, cataract, glaucoma, refractive errors, and diabetic retinopathy and analyze their effects on neural-like feature representations in deep learning models.

pmc-11532032.title: TL-CStrans Net: a vision robot for table tennis player action recognition driven via CS-Transformer
pmc-11532032.creator: Libo Ma, Yan Tong
pmc-11532032.description: Currently, the application of robotics technology in sports training and competitions is rapidly increasing. Traditional methods mainly rely on image or video data, neglecting the effective utilization of textual information. To address this issue, we propose: TL-CStrans Net: A vision robot for table tennis player action recognition driven via CS-Transformer.

pmc-11647828.title: Investigating the biodiversity conservation capability of technological innovation and FinTech
pmc-11647828.creator: Shayan Khan Kakar, Jing Wang, Noman Arshed, Tran Thi Le Hien, Nazir Muhammad Abdullahi
pmc-11647828.description: Human activities, primarily economic growth, and technological innovation, threaten global biodiversity. This study utilizes 22-year panel data from 87 developing countries and a novel cross-sectional heterogeneous factor analysis-based financial technology index to investigate how economic growth, renewable energy consumption, technological innovation, natural resources, and financial technology affect biodiversity.

pmc-12576981.creator: Yue Yin, Qiang Fang, Zhu Min, Ting Liu
pmc-12576981.description: ObjectiveTo understand the 2024 health-literacy level of college students majoring in sports in China—covering the three dimensions of basic knowledge and beliefs, healthy lifestyles and behaviors, and fundamental health skills, as well as the six domains of scientific health perspectives, communicable disease prevention, chronic disease prevention, safety and first aid, basic medical care, and health-information literacy—and to identify their determinants,

pmc-12604224.title: Epigenetic regulation of NR5A2 influences colorectal cancer cell stemness via a stemness-related transcription factor NANOG
pmc-12604224.creator: Jia Liu, Li Li, Liang Zhang, Wenpeng Wang, Lei Zheng, Dalu Kong, Jiefu Wang, Yang Zhan
pmc-12604224.description: ObjectiveColorectal cancer (CRC) is an aggressive malignancy with high mortality, and the identification of upstream regulators of stemness represents a critical step toward developing more effective targeted therapies. This study aimed to define the role of NR5A2 in CRC, particularly in the context of cancer stem cells (CSCs).

pmc-12657127.title: A Case Report of Riedel’s Thyroiditis Behaving as Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma: A Rare Presentation
pmc-12657127.creator: Ahmed Lamey, Sherif Farahat, Salma Elsayed, Mark Magdy
pmc-12657127.description: This case report describes a 47-year-old male with a history of hypothyroidism, presenting with a rapidly enlarging neck mass, dysphagia, and dyspnea, raising clinical suspicion for anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC). Initial investigations, including post-contrast CT and fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC), were inconclusive but suggested a possible malignant etiology.

pmc-12751391.title: Left ventricular hypertrabeculation is a novel predictor of life-threatening arrhythmic events in long QT syndrome patients
pmc-12751391.creator: Jing Yang, Kun Li, Fang Liu, Lingyun Kong, Yuanwei Liu, Fei She, Rong He, Tingting Lv, Fulan Liu, Ping Zhang
pmc-12751391.description: BackgroundLong QT syndrome (LQTS) is a malignant cardiac channelopathy for patients with traditionally normal heart structures. Sporadic cases reported left ventricular hypertrabeculation (LVHT) was a deadly double hit in LQTS patients. Here we summarize the prevalence of LVHT within LQTS subjects and analyse the correlation of LVHT with life-threatening arrhythmic events (LAEs).

pmc-12756105.title: Unusually low infection rate of Dirofilaria immitis in its wildlife hosts by the northern border of the Mediterranean climate zone in Hungary
pmc-12756105.creator: Eszter Nagy, Rebeka Ráhel Nagy, Ágnes Csivincsik, Tibor Halász, Sibusiso Moloi, Melinda Kovács, Gábor Nagy, Tamás Tari
pmc-12756105.description: Wildlife-originating zoonotic pathogens represent a special form of human-wildlife conflict. Disease spillover and spillback can cause health damage to both sides. Canine heartworm (Dirofilaria immitis) is considered a climate-sensitive parasite due to the special environmental demands of its mosquito vectors.

pmc-12969408.creator: Francesco Smeraglia, Lucian Lior Marcovici, Morena Anna Basso, Alessio Bernasconi, Andrea Cozzolino, Giovanni Balato

pmc-12988104.title: Cognitive architecture and behavioral model based on social evidence and resource constraints
pmc-12988104.creator: Anton Kolonin
pmc-12988104.description: The cognitive architecture presented in this paper is expected to be able to explain certain aspects of human behavior, guide the development of artificial intelligence agents, and align the behavioral patterns of the latter with the former. The architecture is based on the principle of social proof or social evidence, including the principle of resource constraints.

pmc-13208997.title: Gravity-Driven Microfluidic Viscosity Measurement with a Small Capillary Radius and Strong Pinning Effect
pmc-13208997.creator: Jian Dong, Bilong Liu, Xuxuan Ai, Qihang Zhang
pmc-13208997.description: In this study, we introduce a novel method for microscale viscosity measurement that eliminates the need for direct contact angle determination. By utilizing a capillary with a sufficiently small radius (R < 0.2 mm), the sharp outlet edge pins the three-phase contact line, stabilizing the apparent contact angle near 90° and nullifying the capillary pressure term.

pmc-13385603.title: Salt-associated angina bullosa haemorrhagica in a child: A case report with literature review
pmc-13385603.creator: Khlood A. Alkurdi, Jihad A. Alokaily, Sara D. Alzanbaqi, Hassan H. Alamer, Jawaher M. Alotaibi, Abdullah F. Alshammari
pmc-13385603.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Angina bullosa haemorrhagica is a rare, benign, self-limiting oral mucosal disorder characterised by the sudden appearance of blood-filled bullae in the absence of systemic or haematological abnormalities. Paediatric cases remain exceptionally uncommon. This report describes a 5-year-old Saudi Arabian boy who presented with multiple painless haemorrhagic oral bullae after ingesting natural salt crystals during a visit to a salt lake in Al-Qassim, Saudi Arabia.

pmc-13434141.title: Hypnosis and relaxation techniques in the management of temporomandibular disorders: a scoping review
pmc-13434141.creator: Estelle Casazza, Benoit Ballester, Maxime Joncour, Yamina Benamara-Tlemsani, Jean-Philippe Ré, Anne Giraudeau
pmc-13434141.description: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are common causes of orofacial pain, influenced by psychological and behavioural factors. Non-pharmacological interventions, such as hypnosis and relaxation techniques, have been proposed to modulate pain perception, reduce muscle hyperactivity, and improve coping. However, their role in TMD management remains unclear.
